title: Layered multi-arch airgap bundles + kube-distro overlay support
author: Anya Patel
description: Motivation: Customers running air-gapped Private deployments want smaller, incremental OCI bundles that support multiple CPU architectures (x86_64, arm64) and per-distro overlays (kubeadm, rke2, k3s) so upgrades and node replacements can consume only the layers required for their platform. This PR introduces a layered multi-arch bundle format + a lightweight overlay system that applies runtime distro-specific patches during installation. Key changes: 1) new layered OCI index generator that produces per-arch index manifests and a top-level umbrella index; 2) delta snapshot metadata that allows clients to fetch only changed layers for incremental updates; 3) distro overlay manifests (kubeadm-1.26, rke2-1.23, k3s-1.28) with small systemd unit drop-ins and CRI shim config fixes; 4) installer changes to resolve and validate the layered index, apply overlays atomically, and provide an explicit rollback path. Checklist: - [x] implement layered OCI index generator - [x] add per-arch delta metadata and verifier - [x] add distro overlays and examples - [x] wire installer to apply overlays in airgap mode - [x] tests: unit + e2e airgap multi-arch smoke - [x] document format and migration steps Docs: docs/airgap/multi-arch-bundle.md includes format, migration strategy, and example commands. Migration notes: existing single-index bundles remain supported; migrate by generating layered index with --umbrella flag and distributing the umbrella index plus arch-specific OCI blobs. Rollback: installer writes a snapshot manifest before apply and will attempt to restore previous manifest + layers if any overlay post-apply check fails. Security: signed index support enforced in CI and verified at install time (cosign v2). Related: complements ENG-7891 (airgap distribution improvements) and OPS-402 (onboarding requirements for arm64 fleets).

review_comments: Marco Nguyen: Nice work. Two questions: (1) can we avoid shipping duplicate layers between x86/arm if the blob checksum matches? (2) overlay_applier needs clearer failure semantics so we don't leave half-applied state.

Anya Patel: For (1) the layered index deduplicates by digest and only references shared blobs from multiple arch entries; generator uses content-addressing so duplicates are avoided. For (2) installer now writes a pre-apply snapshot and uses atomic rename for active-manifest; failure will trigger rollback and we added verification checks post-apply.
Liam O'Connor: Please add unit tests covering signature verification path; I saw CI flake on cosign verification once.
Anya Patel: Added signature verification test and extended CI job to run cosign verify using offline keyring in test harness.
Rina Shah: Approving the approach, but please include a short note in release notes about the new umbrella index format and migration command.
Anya Patel: Added release notes and a migration example in docs/multi-arch-bundle.md

release_notes: Added layered multi-arch airgap bundle format and distro-specific overlay support. Customers can generate an umbrella index to serve both x86_64 and arm64 with deduplicated layers. Installer applies overlays atomically and will rollback on failure. See docs/airgap/multi-arch-bundle.md for migration steps and examples.
